articles.title: I Finally Found My Dream Collectible, and It Only Took 40 Years of Searching for It
articles.summary: Not to date myself, but it was, oh, 40 years ago or so when I first watched the now mostly forgotten TV show Voyagers! as a kid. A time-travel romp with an occasionally steampunk vibe, the short-lived series featured a kid as one half of its time-hopping duo, so the self-identification factor was…
body: But the real appeal of Voyagers! for me was in the time-travel mechanism that the Voyagers like Bogg used: the Omni. For whatever reason, this thing really hit me where I lived.

Is it perfect? No. Is it an affordable chance to have a semi-forgotten piece of TV history displayed on my book shelf? Heck yeah, it is. While the prop replica is mostly made of resin, unlike the more expensive version currently available which is brass (and runs over $1000 now), the dials on this piece are actually brass and do in fact rotate. The lid flips open as well, and there’s a belt clip if you plan on cosplaying as Bogg (or Jeffrey). The lights don’t blink and it doesn’t emit any sounds either, but again… for me this is a display piece that falls right in my price range.

But hey, if they ever add an actual time-travel chip to it, maybe I’ll eventually spring for the more expensive version that’s floating around out there. Until then… as Bogg used to say, green light, kid. We did it!
Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social, or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3. Or do both!

articles.title: Rockstar Games Finally Addresses Extraordinary and 'Heartbreaking' GTA 6 Leaks, Warns Players That 'Some Spoilers' May Now Impact 'The Intended Game Experience'
articles.summary: Rockstar Games has finally addressed the past week's extraordinary spate of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks, describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans.
body: In a statement posted to social media, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers", but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

The past week has seen more than a dozen gameplay clips appear online, posted by an individual or group that has claimed to be leaking material to highlight the death of physical media and the impact this will have on game ownership, while also charging fans to vote on further leaks using cryptocurrency, in what is widely-seen as a money-making exercise.

Today's statement by Rockstar makes no mention of its efforts to try and stop these leaks from occuring, or the legal processes it has begun to try and determine the identity of the leaker(s). Indeed, the statement could be read as an admission that the leaks will likely continue — and worsen, with story spoilers likely — at least in the short term.

articles.title: The Biggest Gaming Stories That Happened Since GTA 5 Came Out 13 Years Ago
articles.summary: The long, long wait for GTA 6 is coming to an end, as the game's November 19 release date approaches. Yes, there have been many leaks, but the genuine article arrives soon. It's been 13 years since GTA 5 launched in September 2013, and a lot has happened in the world of video games since then.
body: In this post, we're running through some of the most notable gaming events and stories since GTA 5 launched more than a decade ago. To be sure, this is not an exhaustive list, and it does not touch on the many real-world, non-gaming high-profile events that have transpired. This list is all about big gaming stories, of which there have been many.

The COVID-19 pandemic, which took hold in early 2020, had a massive impact on the world, of course, including the video game industry. Due to stay-at-home orders and general social distancing policies, people spent more time--and money--on things they could do at home. Naturally, home gym and fitness equipment sales soared, but so did spending on entertainment like video games.

articles.title: Marvel Fans Say Avengers: Endgame Encore's Extra 4 Minutes Risk Being 'Really Oversold', After Directors Insist Movie is 'Required Viewing for Following The Story in Doomsday'
articles.summary: We all love Avengers: Endgame, but some Marvel fans are now suggesting that the four minutes of footage added to its upcoming Encore re-release risk being oversold by its directors.
body: Endgame is one of the best Marvel movies of all time — perhaps the best — and so it's not surprising to see it return to theaters this fall ahead of Avengers: Doomsday's arrival. Not only will this new chance to watch the film inject a few more million into its box office total (perhaps enough to overtake Avatar once again!), the experience will likely remind cinema audiences of the excitement felt at the close of the Infinity Saga, as a decade of storytelling came to a natural conclusion.

But after the reveal that Avengers: Endgame Encore will be just four minutes longer than the movie's original runtime, fans are revisiting recent comments by directors Joe and Anthony Russo — who suggested that an Endgame watch (or rewatch) was "required viewing" to follow Doomsday's own story — with a healthy dose of scepticism.

A clip of the Russos discussing Avengers: Endgame Encore at San Diego Comic-Con last month is now being shared widely on social media, where the duo discussed why they thought fans should see the film again with Fandango.

articles.title: A Beloved Critical Role Cast Member Will Probably Miss Campaign 4 for a Long Time
articles.summary: From the moment Critical Role 's Campaign 4 was introduced with its 13-player cast, it was clear that Dungeon Master Brennan Lee Mulligan would not pull his punches with them. This became even clearer during Campaign 4's 30th episode, "Here in the Dark."
body: After a valiant battle against the undead, Teor Pridesire (Travis Willingham) perished alongside his brother Cyd in the crypts of the Tachonis estate. Willingham didn't appear in episode 31, the final episode of the arc before Campaign 4 went on break for Age of Umbra: Sallowlands. Many fans were already hyped at the thought of Travis' new character appearing in the next arc, which debuted on Aug. 27.

However, thanks to Critical Role’s talk-show, Tale Gate, hosted by Whitney Moore (who plays Tyranny in Campaign 4) and featuring several guests, we now know that Willingham’s return to the Campaign 4 cast might take much longer than fans expected.

Speaking in the Beacon-exclusive segment Night Cap, Willingham took the opportunity to answer a fan who wondered when he would next appear. “I genuinely don’t have a backup character planned yet. I also don’t have a reentry point planned yet,” Willingham explained. “I feel like if you die, you got to get punished.”

Tomorrow's Netflix extended look has likewise "taken longer than we wanted to get it ready". "As with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve," the statement went on.

"We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week - your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games," the statement concludes.

articles.title: Crimson Desert Enhanced is a free upgrade that's out now and revamps the story, adds new skills and comes with all previously-released updates
articles.summary: Crimson Desert Enhanced was among the more surprising reveals of Gamescom Opening Night Live. Not because it was a trailer for a game that's already available, but that it was justified when the trailer ran through the new additions in Enhanced.
body: Crimson Desert Enhanced is a multi-fold upgrade. This version includes everything up to this week's 2.00 patch; that is all previous updates and post-launch additions. It also adds new stuff across the entire game, in the form of story cutscenes, more narrative moments, new skills and more.

Developer Pearl Abyss is seemingly so confident in these narrative upgrades that Enhanced launches localised in five new voice languages: German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Japanese. It also includes Arabic subtitles and user interface text.

Among the upgrades featured in the new update and Enhanced are new skills you can equip. In fact, the skill system has been overhauled. Abyss Link has been added as a new resource you can spend on learning skills. This is tied to Abyss Artifacts, and when you use one, your other characters will be awarded Abyss Links to invest in learning skills.

Each character has their own Abyss Links inventory, meaning you can have different builds without affecting each other, and you can reset skill progression individually, too. This refunds all previously used Abyss Links.
points: Crimson Desert Enhanced was among the more surprising reveals of Gamescom Opening Night Live.

articles.title: Having played it, Tides of Annihilation looks to be a flashy, combo-heavy game of Simon Says
articles.summary: Tides of Annihilation is a very stylish, combo-heavy, Simon Says game. It's a mishmash of mythologies and action game tropes, and while I feel as though its teeters on the edge of messiness, it proved quite the thrill on the Gamescom show floor.
body: Tides is, most apparently, a strange and enamouring game to look at. It's the Homer Simpson makeup shotgun of aesthetics. I found myself wandering around a ruined museum, assailed by giant knights and Egyptian beasts. My mentor is a Chinese saint of martial prowess. My character is a British lady called Gwendolyn with a gaggle of Arthurian knights she can summon to her aid. The buffet approach to worldbuilding is a bold choice, but it allows for truly absurd visual clashes that if nothing else sets the game apart from its contemporaries.

The demo I played was split into four parts: a basic tutorial, a slice of an early-game level, a boss fight, and a supposedly challenging bonus boss battle. Plenty to do, though I was heavily encouraged to put the game on the "story" difficulty, which I fear prevented me from seeing the game's true fangs.
points: Tides of Annihilation is a very stylish, combo-heavy, Simon Says game.
It's a mishmash of mythologies and action game tropes, and while I feel as though its teeters on the edge of messiness, it proved quite the thrill on the Gamescom show floor.

articles.title: Apex Legends is getting 'fatal error' crashes with RX 9070 XT GPUs, but there is a workaround
articles.summary: Apex Legends seems to be having trouble working with the AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT right now. As relayed by the Apex Legends account ApexCommunityJP on X (machine translated), "We have confirmed an issue causing crashes for players using the AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT GPU, and we are currently investigating…
body: I can confirm on my end that Apex Legends crashes when I try to launch it using a rig with an RX 9070 XT. I get the following game/engine 'fatal error': "The application's device failed due to badly formed commands sent by the application. This is a design-time issue that should be investigated and fixed."
The aforementioned X account does recommend trying to roll back your AMD graphics driver; however, some replies to this claim that doing so doesn't resolve the problem.

One suggestion in the replies that does seem to have worked for me as a temporary workaround is to add the following to the game's Steam launch options: "+staticprop_color_use_bindless 0 +staticprop_depth_use_bindless 0 +r_drawworld_depth_bindless 0". To do so, on the game's Steam page, click the cog, then Properties, then paste those commands into the launch options.

articles.title: Path of Exile 2 finally has its 1.0 release date and it's coming this year
articles.summary: Grinding Gear Games made a surprise Path of Exile 2 announcement at Gamescom Opening Night Live yesterday. The developer confirmed when the game's long-awaited 1.0 release will be.
body: Path of Exile 2 leaves early access 11th December, which is also when the game will be available as a free-to-play game, dropping the nominal charge for the Founder's Pack requirement it currently has - the only way into the early access version.

The 1.0 release introduces a new class in the Duelist, a melee-focused character and strangely the game's first sword-wielding class. The Duelist can also use shields and is designed for aggressive combat. The two remaining campaign Acts will also be part of the 1.0 launch, completing the campaign.

The Path of Exile 2 full release arrives almost exactly two years after the initial early access launch. The 1.0 date has been something of a moving target, though the developer did say earlier this year that it's aiming to launch it sometime after November's ExileCon Path of Exile convention.
